title: Your Hourly Rate vs the nbl Average Salary: Annual, Fortnightly and Super Explained
description: Compare your hourly rate to the nbl average salary using our 38‑hour week formula. Includes casual loading, super on top, and tax estimates for 2026–27.
salarySummary: Based on a 38‑hour week, the nbl average salary (national baseline average from ABS data) is about $108,352 per year before tax, but your actual pay depends on your hourly rate, casual loading, and super.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52. For a standard full‑time worker, that’s hourly × 38 × 52. For example, $30 per hour gives $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280 per year. If you’re casual, add 25% loading first: $30 × 1.25 = $37.50 per hour, then $37.50 × 38 × 52 = $74,100. Super is paid on top of your ordinary earnings (including casual loading) at 12%.

faqs.q: What is casual loading and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. It is part of your ordinary earnings, so super is calculated on the loaded rate. The National Minimum Wage for casuals from 1 July 2026 is $33.05 per hour (base $26.44 + 25%). Always enter your base rate in the timesheet; tick the casual box to add loading automatically.

faqs.q: Does the nbl average salary include super?
faqs.a: No, the nbl average salary (based on ABS Average Weekly Earnings of $2,083.70 per week for full‑time adult ordinary time) is gross pay before tax and before super. Super is paid on top by your employer at 12% of your ordinary earnings, up to the $270,830 maximum contribution base. So your total employment cost is higher than the salary figure.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the nbl Average Salary and Your Pay

When you’re comparing a job offer or checking your current rate, the **nbl average salary** (national baseline average) provides a useful benchmark. According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics, full‑time adult ordinary time earnings averaged $2,083.70 per week in May 2026. That’s about $108,352 per year for a 38‑hour week. But remember: this is an average across all industries and occupations, not the median for your specific job. Your own pay will depend on your hourly rate, whether you’re permanent or casual, and any award or agreement conditions.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly × Hours × 52

To turn your hourly rate into an annual figure, use the simple formula:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

This calculator assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For a standard full‑time employee, we use 38 hours per week – the common ordinary hours under many awards. If you work different hours, adjust accordingly. For example, a part‑timer working 20 hours a week at $30 per hour earns $30 × 20 × 52 = $31,200 per year.

### Casual Loading: 25% on Top

If you’re a casual employee, you’re entitled to a 25% loading on your base hourly rate. This compensates for not receiving paid sick leave or annual leave. The loading is part of your ordinary earnings, so your super guarantee is calculated on the loaded rate. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading – use the checkbox on [the timesheet](/) to add it automatically.

Example: Base rate $26.44 (National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026). With casual loading: $26.44 × 1.25 = $33.05 per hour. Annual for 38 hours: $33.05 × 38 × 52 = $65,306.80. Super at 12% on top: $7,836.82, making total employment cost $73,143.62.

### Fortnightly Pay: A Handy Figure

Many employers pay fortnightly. To get your gross fortnightly pay, multiply your weekly pay by 2. Using the example above: weekly pay for a casual on minimum wage is $33.05 × 38 = $1,255.90. Fortnightly: $2,511.80. This helps you budget and compare with advertised salaries.

### Award Rates vs National Minimum Wage

The National Minimum Wage ($26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026) is the legal floor. However, most employees are covered by an award or registered agreement that sets higher minimum rates. Always check your specific award – you can find links to [pay guides](/blog) on our site. Award rates often include classifications for different skill levels and may have penalty rates for weekends or nights. The nbl average salary is much higher than the minimum because it reflects the mix of all full‑time workers, including those on higher pay.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Your employer must pay super guarantee contributions of 12% of your ordinary time earnings, on top of your gross salary. This applies to both permanent and casual employees. The maximum earnings base for super is $270,830 per year (2026–27). If your annual ordinary earnings exceed that, super only applies up to that cap. Super is not deducted from your pay – it’s an additional cost to your employer. So when you see a salary offer, remember that the total employment cost is salary plus 12% super.

### Tax Estimates for 2026–27

Tax is withheld from your pay using the resident tax scales. For 2026–27:
- Nil tax on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (generally). The tax‑free threshold is included. If you earn less than the tax‑free threshold, you may not need to pay tax. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide for a more detailed estimate, but remember this is not a tax determination.

### How to Use the Timesheet Calculator

Our [the timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate and toggle casual loading. It shows your annual, monthly, fortnightly, and weekly gross pay, plus estimated tax and super. It’s designed for quick comparisons. For example, if you’re offered a salary of $80,000 per year, you can work backwards: $80,000 ÷ 52 ÷ 38 ≈ $40.49 per hour. Then compare that to your current rate or the nbl average salary.

### The nbl Average Salary in Context

The nbl average salary of $108,352 per year (based on ABS full‑time adult ordinary time earnings) is a broad average. It includes all full‑time employees – from entry‑level to executives. Your job may pay more or less. For a more targeted comparison, look at industry‑specific averages from the ABS or your award. Remember: this is an average, not a median. Half of full‑time workers earn less than the median, which is typically lower than the average due to high earners pulling the average up.

### Casual Loading and Super: Key Takeaways

- Casual loading (25%) is added to your base rate before calculating annual pay and super.
- Super (12%) is paid on top of your ordinary earnings, including casual loading.
- The nbl average salary is gross before super and tax.
- Use the formula hourly × hours × 52, assuming 38 hours for full‑time unless otherwise stated.

For more details, see our pages on [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) and [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging). You can also explore [average pay](/topics/average-pay) for industry benchmarks.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay shown here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax‑free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
